title: Bot Crossing visual and behavior corpus
scope: Reference-derived character direction for original Sower prototypes; not a product recreation or measured style classifier.

sources.observation: Two small white robot-like astronauts on a tiled sci-fi world. Each has a round white helmet/body mass, glossy black circular face screen, tiny white curved eyes and smile, a short thin crown antenna ending in a white ball, rounded short limbs, and soft toy-like proportions. Background includes turquoise machinery and white/red structures.

Separate Sowers Scout character anchor: cream body, vivid orange crown stripe and side panels, cocoa-brown visor, simple cream smiling eyes, compact rounded body and limbs. Its candy study is an orange gummy concept. Retain this palette and approachable helper personality as a preference; no color ratios or Bot Crossing attribution inferred.

Official page describes a 3D world where bots work across projects; a bot needing a decision raises a question mark and waves; users can click bots to chat. It describes persistent project plots and a flyable world. This supports role and motion affordances, not detailed character geometry.

Local implementation builds procedural helmet, visor, face, pack, antenna, tip and lamp around an animated crew rig; supports state trims, status faces, walking/running, working, waving, and attention badge behavior. This corroborates this clone's implementation only, not every public or commercial Bot Crossing version.
Local face atlas includes idle, blink, happy, work, thinking, wait, alert, error, sleep, wink, love, cheer, boot and sad expression frames.
Local rig maps idle, walking, running, hammering, working, cheering, jump, wave, sit, hit, spawn and interact clips; the mannequin head is omitted in favor of the custom helmet/face.

traits.evidence: In goat3, two characters read as compact upright figures, with large round head/helmet masses and smaller bodies; the white silhouette remains legible against dark blue floor.
traits.sower_translation: Build an original seedling-sized helper with an oversized rounded hood/head and a short, stable body; keep the silhouette readable at thumbnail scale.

blend.high: Use the large-head/small-body ratio as a broad proportion cue.
blend.medium: Combine with Mars suit utility while retaining soft toy proportions.
blend.low: Avoid copying the specific helmet outline or exact body proportions.

traits.evidence: Goat3 shows a smooth, nearly spherical white helmet shell; no hard panel seams are prominent at this viewing size.
traits.sower_translation: Prefer a smooth, softly beveled protective hood with one or two original broad seams, not a detailed replica.

blend.high: Retain one smooth protective head enclosure.
blend.medium: Use soft hood volume with a distinctive agricultural brim or seed pod contour.
blend.low: Drop helmet mimicry and use a fabric cowl or leaf hood.

traits.evidence: Each goat3 face is a dark, nearly circular glossy screen inset in the white helmet, with high-contrast white marks.
traits.sower_translation: Use a small dark face window or seed-sensor panel with expressive, simple marks; design its shape and bezel originally.

blend.high: A high-contrast expressive face panel is a useful broad cue.
blend.medium: Translate into a dark soil-sensor window with botanical eye motifs.
blend.low: Use a non-screen embroidered or sculpted face.

traits.evidence: The visible faces show two upward-curving eye marks and a small curved smile, conveying friendly attention rather than realism.
traits.sower_translation: Give the helper a readable, optimistic expression using a few broad shapes; support alternate curious, focused and sleepy expressions.

blend.medium: Mix an upbeat default with Wobbly-like slapstick reactions.
blend.low: Avoid screen-face graphics; express emotion through posture and carved features.

traits.evidence: Both goat3 characters have a thin stalk rising from the helmet crown and a small spherical tip.
traits.sower_translation: If useful, use one thick, short sprout-like sensor with a broad tip; keep it robust and avoid a fragile thin stalk.

blend.high: A single crown marker may communicate helper identity.
blend.medium: Replace the antenna with a sturdy leaf or seedling nub.

traits.risk: Thin stalks and tiny tips can read as fragile, disappear at small sizes, and create candy demolding or breakage problems.

traits.evidence: The lower white mass is compact and rounded, visually continuous with the suit; a small dark circular chest mark is visible on one figure.
traits.sower_translation: Make a compact rounded tunic/torso with a large simple chest emblem such as a seed, leaf, or pocket, leaving broad uninterrupted surfaces.

blend.high: Use a compact torso with one clear chest focal point.
blend.medium: Add a work apron or seed pouch as an original gardening adaptation.
blend.low: Use layered clothing shapes instead of a suit-like body.

traits.evidence: Arms and legs in goat3 appear short, rounded and separated into soft limb forms. The still does not establish joint mobility or range.
traits.sower_translation: Propose original short, soft limbs with mitten hands and broad boots. Any articulation, elbow or knee design is a new Sower implementation choice.

blend.high: Short, soft limbs create a cute helper read.
blend.medium: Use flexible limbs for physical comedy while retaining mitten hands.
blend.low: Use root-like feet and broader leaf-shaped hands.

traits.evidence: Goat4 (not the Bot Crossing still) shows cream, orange and cocoa as the user's preferred character palette; goat3 itself appears predominantly white with black face screens.
traits.sower_translation: Treat cream/orange/cocoa as a separate Sowers preference anchor. Map cream to the main body, orange to one or two broad accents, and cocoa to the face window only as a qualitative direction; do not claim measured ratios.

blend.high: Keep the separate Goat4 cream/orange/cocoa palette invariant; change form and pose rather than source palette.
blend.medium: Keep the separate Goat4 cream/orange/cocoa palette invariant; change form and pose rather than source palette.
blend.low: Keep the separate Goat4 cream/orange/cocoa palette invariant; change form and pose rather than source palette.

traits.evidence: The still is small and softly rendered; broad smooth masses dominate, while tiny joints and chest marks are secondary.
traits.sower_translation: Favor clean matte surfaces, rounded edges and a few large details. Do not spend silhouette budget on tiny bolts, seams or small text.

blend.high: Keep broad clean surfaces and sparse accents.
blend.medium: Add tactile fabric or planted-seed texture only in larger readable zones.
blend.low: Use handcrafted surface texture but keep micro-detail out.

traits.risk: Very small raised marks can vanish in candy and add weak, thin features that are difficult to demold.

traits.evidence: The smiling, tiny astronaut forms in goat3 read as cheerful companions; this is inferred from the still, not a Bot Crossing product promise.
traits.sower_translation: Make the character a patient, curious garden helper: pleased to notice progress, calm when waiting, and gently alert when a choice is needed.

blend.medium: Add playful clumsiness without making the helper seem careless.
blend.low: Make the role quiet and contemplative, with warmth in pose rather than a grin.

traits.evidence: Official product page says a bot needing a decision raises a question mark above its head and starts waving to get attention.
traits.sower_translation: Prototype a clear pause-and-wave pose with a broad, detachable-looking sprout/question cue; Sower may use a leaf-shaped attention marker rather than a copied icon.

blend.medium: Use a raised leaf or hand gesture, with no floating punctuation.
blend.low: Use a planted sign or head tilt instead of waving.

traits.evidence: Local astronaut rig provides walk/run and hammering/working loops; astronauts can move around their project site. This is local implementation evidence, not an official claim about all product versions.
traits.sower_translation: Allow broad walk, carry, tend and pause poses; any tool should be oversized, blunt, and original to the garden role.

blend.high: A visible hand-work loop supports a productive helper identity.
blend.medium: Translate hammering to watering, tending or seed placement.
blend.low: Keep hands empty; communicate work through purposeful travel and inspection.

traits.evidence: Local face atlas supports distinct idle, blink, happy, work, think, wait, alert, error, sleep, wink, love, cheer, boot and sad states.
traits.sower_translation: Plan a small set of face states with chunky marks: content, curious, focused, waiting, surprised and tired. Treat these as animation opportunities, not mandatory facial decals.

blend.high: Use expression changes to make work state readable.
blend.medium: Combine screen expressions with body acting and Wobbly-like surprise.
blend.low: Keep face fixed and let silhouette/gesture carry emotion.

traits.evidence: Official page describes orbit-to-plot navigation. Multi-scale character readability is our design inference and test requirement, not an official character specification.
traits.sower_translation: Prioritize a distinct head-body outline, one broad color block and one clear gesture; keep important identity cues visible when reduced.

blend.high: Use one or two large identifiers instead of fine detail.
blend.medium: Let the garden tool or leaf crest act as the distant identifier.
blend.low: Simplify to a distinct silhouette without reliance on a face display.

unknowns: The goat3 still is user-supplied imagery, not independently verified official Bot Crossing key art; exact origin/version is unknown.
The official page supports behavior and world context but its accessible text does not establish exact bot mesh geometry, material values, proportions or rig design.
Local source code describes this repository's implementation only. It must not be treated as a complete representation of the commercial service or every product revision.
No physical dimensions, material measurements, palette ratios, manufacturing tests, or candy tolerances are established by this corpus.
originality_and_candy_notes: Use references for broad visual principles only; do not copy the Bot Crossing mesh, exact face, helmet, pack, antenna, insignia, or source assets.
Keep any future candy study as a concept image, not manufacturing evidence.
Avoid thin antennae, narrow limb gaps, tiny knobs, floating fine details and deep narrow undercuts; favor rounded, connected masses and broad raised marks.
Goat4 cream/orange/cocoa and its helper character remain a separate user preference anchor; no measured palette share is inferred.
